Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase. The Sri Lankan players make their way out into the middle and are followed by the West Indian openers, Evin Lewis and Shai Hope. Nuwan Pradeep to begin proceedings with the ball now. Here he comes...

The target is not a big one! Windies should back themselves to chase this down. However, it will all depend on how they play spin. Lanka, n the other hand, needs wickets at regular intervals. Join us for the second essay in a bit.

Jason Holder is in for a chat! He says that there was some indiscipline on their part but they were good at the start and they faltered slightly and they were made to pay. Says that the total is good enough to chase and they are rearing to go. Feels that the batters have to come on out and put their hands up and chase this total down.

The Windies bowling was not that great, to begin with! They were way too short at the start. They though did really well after they got the first wicket. They were gifted a couple of wickets in the form of run outs but overall, they bowled decently. It is difficult to pick one bowler as there were a few bowlers who did a good job but if one has to be picked, it has to be Jason Holder.

A fine, fine effort by Windies with the ball! They will be pretty pleased with where they stand in the game at the moment, especially after the opening stand the Lankans had. After electing to bat, the visitors got off to a flier courtesy their openers. Both scored half tons and added 105. However, once Karunaratne fell, the procession started. At one stage even 200 looked out of reach but the debutant, Bandara, played a superb hand, a fifty on debut and gave his bowlers something to bowl at.

OUT! CAUGHT! Joseph finishes things off with a wicket and this will give him some confidence. On a good length and around off, Nuwan Pradeep makes some room and looks to play a big shot but does not time this one well. The ball loops towards the mid off region, where Romario Shepherd does well to keep his eyes on the ball, and then take the catch. SRI LANKA ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 232!
Width on offer as this one is outside off, good length, worked through point for one.
This is a fuller ball down the leg side, LS leaves. Wide signalled.
Good length on off, blocked out.

FOUR! A welcome boundary and Sandakan is getting his groove on now. Length and around off, Lakshan Sandakan slams this in the gap between deep square leg and deep mid-wicket. Takes a couple of bounces and goes past the ropes.
Slapped to the deep cover fielder and the batters exchange ends now.
Around off on a good length, LS clears his front foot and slams this one towards the long off region, for a single.
Around off, good length, well blocked out. Jason Holder finishes with figures of 10-1-39-2. A very good show for him.
On off, kept out.
Nuwan Pradeep is the last man in!

OUT! CAUGHT! A simple catch Bandara goes back after getting his fifty. A little too high for Bandara and he gives an easy catch to the mid-wicket fielder. Slightly short and around off, Bandara looks to get on top of the bounce but fails to do so and only manages to give a simple catch to Akeal Hosein at mid-wicket. Only one more wicket needed now.
Worked to fine leg for one run.

FIFTY FOR ASHEN BANDARA! A very good one by the youngster and he will be very happy to starrt off his international career with a fifty! Only the 5th Sri Lankan to acheive this feat. Shortish and around off, pulled to deep square leg for one.

RUN OUT CHANCE MISSED! Short, outside off, tapped towards covers and the fielders take off for the single. Pollard comes ahead and collects the ball and throws it towards Alzarri Joseph, but he is not able to collect it nicely. One run.
A full toss down the leg side, Bandara leaves it alone. No signal of wide from the umpire and so maybe it took the thigh pad and went to the keeper.
On a shorter length and around off, LS again swivels and pulls this one firmly to deep square leg for one run.
Short ball around off, LS pulls this one to mid-wicket.
Around off, played towards mid off.

Edgy four! A top edge and a four. Not what he wanted to do, but the boundary will make the Lankans feel good. Shortish, around off, Lakshan Sandakan swipes across the line and the ball takes the top edge, flies over the slip region, into the third man fence.
Back of a length ball outside off, worked through backward point for a single.
Slower bouncer on middle, LS sits under this one.
Low full toss on off, pushed back to the bowler.
Around off, length, worked towards mid on.
Pushed to covers for a single.
Shortish outside off, pulled away to deep mid-wicket for one.
On the pads, worked to the on side.
BEATEN! A dot to end which means Bandara fails to retain strike! Shorter and outside off, Bandara is beaten as he tries to cut.
Shorter and outside off, Bandara cuts but fails to beat point. A little to the left or the right and it would have been a boundary.
Sandakan takes one! Shorter and on off, LS plays it nicely. Hops and guides it through point for one.
TWO LEG BYES! A low full toss on the pads, Joseph does not get his line right. It hits the pad, Hope fails to collect it cleanly. Two taken. leg byes.
BEATEN! Fuller and outside off, Sandakan ends up driving outside the line. It goes past his inside edge.
Outside off, Bandara guides it down to third man for one. So a single on the first ball, that leaves Sandakan with five balls to face.
Bandara gets a single on the last ball which means he keeps strike. Outside off, this is guided towards third man for one.

NOT OUT! GOING OVER! Windies lose both their reviews! That looked high, to be honest! Not sure why Windies reviewed. This is shortish and on off, it is coming in with the angle. Does stay a little low but still hits Bandara high on the pads as he tries to flick. An appeal and the umpire shakes his head. Holder wants it to be reviewed and Pollard does so. Time for the replays and they show that the on-field call is the right one.
Shorter in length, Sandakan pulls it down to fine leg for one. He is off the mark!
DRS Time! For LBW and Pollard goes for it. Ultra Edge shows a flatline. Ball Tracker shows that the wickets are missing, there was too much height on this. NOT OUT!
Shortish and angled into the pads, Sandakan looks to flick but misses to get hit high on the pads.
Lakshan Sandakan is the new batter in!

OUT! CAUGHT! Chameera is strangled down the leg side! Holder is back and Holder strikes! This is on the body, a rib-tickler! Chameera looks to work it on the leg side but it kisses the glove and goes to the keeper. Can Windies keep Lanka under the 230-run mark? They just need two more wickets.
WIDE AGAIN! Bonus runs these for Lanka! Short and on the body, it is ducked under. Probably wided for height.
WIDE! Down the leg side, Chameera lets it be. Wided.
Short and on middle, this is pulled through square leg for one.
Two taken! A good over this for Lanka! On off, it is pushed off the back foot through covers for two.
FOUR! Swept nicely! 200 up for Lanka! Chameera moves across, this is fired on middle, it is swept through square leg. Boundary.
Misfield and Bandara is off strike! On off, it is pushed to Pollard at covers. He is late in getting down and lets it through. One taken.

NOT OUT! Nothing on Ultra Edge and Windies lose a review! It was more in hope. They would have loved Bandara's wicket right now and they probably took a chance. This is fired full and outside off, Bandara looks to sweep but misses. He seems to have hit the ground. The keeper appeals after taking it. It is a muted one. The umpire turns it down. Hope has a discussion with Pollard and then reviews. Replays roll in and it shows the on-field call is the right one.
Steps out but does not get to the pitch of it. Blocks.
The hosts have taken a review for caught behind! Ultra Edge shows that there was no bat involved. The on-field decision of not out, stays on!
Slows it up, gives it flight and bowls it on off. Bandara adjusts well and pushes it to covers.
Around off, flatter, slashed away to the man at point. Just 3 off this one.
On the middle pole, pushed back to the bowler.
On off, blocked out.
Tossed up outside off, Chameera slices this one through point for a brace.
Outside off, shortish, slapped to point for a single.
Outside off, shortish, punched to covers.
Chameera negotiates the three balls he had to play! On middle, blocked.
Another single as this is pushed towards cover.
On middle, it is pushed to covers.
Swept again! Gets on top of the bounce nicely. Rolls his wrists and hits it through mid-wicket for one.
FOUR! Strikes it really well! The sweep shot is used once again. It is nailed between the fielders in the deep, square leg and mid-wicket. Boundary. Bandara holds the key. Can he take Lanka upto 230?
Angled into the pads, Bandara looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.

A wicket maiden by Mohammad! Once again he beats the outside edge. This lands just outside off and then goes on with the arm again. Chameera is guilty of playing inside the line again. It goes past the outside edge.
Powerplay 3 time! Now, West Indies will be able to have a maximum of 5 fielders outside the 30-yard circle, for the last 10 overs of this innings.
On middle, this is worked to mid-wicket.
On off, defended.
BEATEN AGAIN! On off, that too goes on with the arm. Chameera looks to defend but the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Tossed up outside off, it goes on with the arm. Chameera looks to defend but is beaten.

OUT! TAKEN! Another one bites the dust! Not good from Hasaranga! He probably tried playing an aggressive stroke a little too early. He could have waited. He steps out to this loopy ball around off, gets a little too close to the pitch of the ball. Smashes it hard but does not get the desired elevation. Holder takes a good catch above his head. Sri Lanka would have been relying on this pair to bat them till the 45th over at least but that is not the case. Windies into the bowling all-rounders now.
Who comes out now? Dushmantha Chameera, it is!
Very nicely played! Bandara lets the ball come to him and then just at the end, opens the face of the bat and guides it through backward point for a couple.
Slightly shorter and around off, Hasaranga stays leg side of the ball and guides it through point for one.
Now plays the sweep, controls it, keeps it all along the ground through mid-wicket for one.
Bandara is nimble on his feet, he does not get to the pitch of it. Defends.
Shorter and around off, this is pushed through covers for one.
On middle, this is defended.
Bowling change. Fabian Allen is back on now. 4-0-21-1 so far.
A single now! On middle, this is hit down to long on for one. End of a successful over.

OUT! TAKEN! That is a soft dismissal! Windies continue to take wickets on regular intervals. Full and tossed up outside off this time, Mendis comes down the track but does not get to the pitch of the ball. He looks to push it on the up but does so straight to the man at covers. Allen takes a simple catch. The hosts continue to be on top.
Out comes Wanindu Hasaranga for Sri Lanka!
Two! Shorter and around off, Mendis pushes it through covers. Two taken.
On middle, it is pushed to covers.
Very well fielded! Shorter and around off, this is pushed towards cover. The fielder there dives to his right and saves at least two for his side.
Mendis comes down the track and then eases it down to long off for one.
Flatter and on middle, this is pushed down to long on for one more.
Swept again! It is hit hard through square leg. Only one.
FOUR! Swept and done so brilliantly! This is on the pads, Bandara sweeps it nice and fine and it races away. He really likes playing the sweep and plays it well. Welcome boundary.
Fired on the stumps, this is guided to point.
Mendis misses out! This is well short and on the body, Mendis pulls but towards fine leg for only one.
On the pads, this is worked to square leg.
Slower through the air and on middle, defended.
Good running! The sweep is out again, this is played behind square on the leg side. Two again.
Fumble and two! This is swept towards Lewis at deep square leg. A fumble by him sees the batters take two.
Angled into the pads, Mendis looks to work it on the leg side but misses. It hits the pads and rolls on the leg side for one. Leg bye.
On off, defended.
Outside off, this is pushed through covers for one.
Short, on the pads, worked to square on the leg side.
The sweep is hit through square leg for one. Rotating the strike nicely, in this over.
Floated ball on off, Mendis sweeps this one to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Flatter on middle again, worked behind square on the leg side.
Around off, shortish, nudged to the on side.
This is on middle. Swept away nicely to deep mid-wicket for a single.
A full toss on off, bunted to long on by Ashen for one run. Just 3 runs off this over.
Shortish outside off, cut away to point for one.
Around off, played towards mid on.
Shortish and around off and middle, KM looks to play at this but fails to get bat on ball.
On the pads, clipped to square leg again.
Swept away to the deep square leg region for a single now.
On the leg pole, slightly short, pulled to deep square leg for one.
Around off, length, cut away through point for one run.
On a good length and outside off, left alone by KM.
On the middle pole, short, nudged to square leg for one.
Around off, good length, worked to point.
FOUR! Great timing! Short, on the middle pole, Bandara swivels and hooks this one with power, to the deep square leg fence, for a boundary.
On middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Swept through mid-wicket for one.
On off, defended.
On middle, flicked through the leg side for one.
Kamindu Mendis is the new batter in!

OUT! CAUGHT! A simple catch and Allen has struck. The experienced, Dinesh Chanidmal goes back in a very soft manner. Shortish and outside off, Chandimal looks to guide this one through backward point but fails to keep the ball down. The ball lobs towards the sub fielder, Kyle Mayers, who takes this chance nicely. Five down are the visitors.
On middle, swept away nicely through mid-wicket for a single.
A stifled appeal for LBW but nothing from the umpire. A short of a length and on the pads, DC looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pad. An appeal but this one was heading down leg.
Around off, good length, nudged to the point region and the fielder there overthrows, which allows the batters to take the run on offer.
Around off, length, tapped to the off side now.
Worked through square leg again for one run.
On the pads, worked to the deep square leg region for one.
Back of a length and outside off, worked to backward point.

DRINKS! The Windies have fought back brilliantly and they are slightly ahead in the game at the moment! However, this is a good stand building between Chandimal and Bandara and it is a much-needed one for Sri Lanka. They would hope the two can once again turn the tide into their favor. Windies on the other hand, will hope they can keep picking wickets at regular intervals.
Worked to point for one. 10 off this one.
Brilliant work by Walsh Jr. Shortish outside off, sliced away through backward point and the fielder does well to chase after it and stop it. Three.
Pushed to the leg side for one.

MISFIELD AND FOUR! Very poor work from Evin Lewis and he concedes a boundary. Makes an absolute meal of this. Flighted around off, Bandara sweeps this one to deep square leg where EL misfields and gives a boundary away.
Pushed to covers now.
Floated around off, this is eased towards long off for an easy single.
Fabien Allen is on now!
Around off, short of a length, gently tapped to the off side. Only 3 runs off this over.
Outside off on a length, steered behind point for an easy single.
Good length and on off and middle, flicked to the right of mid on this time.
Shortish and outside off, steered late towards third man for one.
Worked to square leg for one now!
Outside off, good length, slapped to point.
Around off, good length, Chandimal clips this one to deep square leg to collect a single.5 off the 28th over.
Around off, full, pushed back to KP.
Nice shot. Good length, on off and middle, Dinesh Chandimal whips this one through mid-wicket and they settle for the brace.
On off, worked to square leg. One run.
Bandara has hurt his arm! The physio is out! The clash with Lewis might have hurt him.

Around off, back of a length, helped to the square leg region as the batters look to sneak the single. Evin Lewis races in and looks to pick the ball up, but fails to do so and the batters get a lucky escape.
On a good length and on middle, worked to mid-wicket.
Fuller, on middle, clipped through square leg for one.
Connects well with the pull but finds Pollard at mid-wicket.
Shortish on the body again, Chandimal looks to swivel and pull but fails to get any bat on this and goes off his body to short fine leg.
Leg bye. Short, on the body, goes off Bandara's body to square leg for a leg bye.
Good length on middle and leg, helped towards square leg. Ashen looks for the single but Dinesh sends him back. A good decision as this could have been risky.
Shortish and around off now, AB just sways away from the line and lets the ball through to the keeper.
Outside off, length, guided to point. Another good over from the captain of the ship, Kieron Pollard!
A slower ball outside off, DC looks to have a feel of this but he gets beaten all ends up.
Ashen Bandara opens his account in ODI cricket! Shortish around off, tapped to backward point for a quick run.
Around off, shortish, worked to square leg.
Good length on off, played towards mid off.
On off, blocked out.
Around off, pushed to point.
Bandara walks out to bat!

OUT! RUN OUT! Oh my my! Sri Lanka lose their fourth wicket and this was very poor, from their end. The debutant goes back for a very low score and he would not have wanted to get out, in his first game, in such a manner. Back of a length ball around off, Chandimal works this one towards the mid on region and he comes ahead looking for the single. His partner, Pathum Nissanka gets on his bike and races to the other end. After 2 seconds, DC says no and hangs back. There is nothing more that Nissanka can do. Darren Bravo collects the ball and runs to the wickets at the other end, he gives the ball to Akeal Hosein and AH whips the bails off.
Around off, blocked.
Back of a length and around off, DC hops and taps this one to point.
On a shorter length and around off, PN swivels and pulls this one to square leg for one.
FOUR! Not that well played but a boundary nonetheless. Shortish, outside off, Pathum Nissanka hops and slashes this one over the slip cordon, into the ropes at third man.
Outside off, not played at.
On middle, fuller, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.
Slipped down the leg side, wided.
On middle, blocked.
Dinesh Chandimal walks out to bat! He needs to build a partnership with the debutant. Sri Lanka are in trouble here.

OUT! RUN OUT! Another one bites the dust! A good phase of play for the hosts as they are coming back well into the game. The skipper, Pollard is again, the man upon whom, the spotlight is shining. He effects a good run out and the Windies will have their tails up! On a good length and around off and middle, Mathews works this one nicely through the mid-wicket region and the batters take two runs this time. The fielder in the deep, Romario Shepherd, runs to his left, collects the ball and throws it towards Pollard, at the non-striker's end as the batters come back for the third. Pollard collects and whips the bails off as Mathews tries hard to come back in. The third umpire is called for and one replay is enough to see that Angelo's bat was not inside the crease. He walks back now!
Is this another wicket! Run out appeal has been taken upstairs! Windies are celebrating and Mathews seems to be struggling.
Short of a length and on middle, Pathum Nissanka hops and flicks this one away to the leg side for a single.
On a good length and around off, stroked through covers for a single.
WIDE. Slips this one down the leg side now, AM lets it be. Wided by the umpire.
Back of a length and on off, Nissanka guides it to point. This is good from the Windies. They are building pressure on the youngster.
One more short one! Nissanka looks to pull but is beaten for pace.
Plays this one nicely! On off, Nissanka rides on top of the bounce and plays it onto the ground.
A good short one, Nissanka fails to get on top of the bounce, he mistimes his pull on the leg side.
Angled into the pads, this is worked through square leg for one.
Fuller and on middle, this is pushed to mid on.
A huge shout but turned down! Outside off, Nissanka slashes at it but misses. A huge appeal from Pollard but he is the only one doing so.
On the pads, Nissanka works it on the leg side and is eager for one. Is sent back. Pathum needs to calm down. He wants a single of every ball he hits.
Outside off, Mathews pushes it towards cover for one. He is off the mark!
Another one on off, it is kept out.
On middle, this is defended solidly.
Angelo Mathews comes out at Number 4!

OUT! Now then, Gunathilaka has been given the marching orders! He walks away in dismay! A unique way for him to be dismissed and that is probably the only way he seemed like getting out. Windies back into the game as both the set openers are dismissed. Coming to the ball now! It is a slower one outside off, Gunathilaka looks to guide it down to third man but gets an underedge. It rolls on the wicket. Gunthilaka takes a start and Nissanka takes off. He is though sent back. Pollard hares after the ball. Gunathilaka kicks the ball away from Pollard as he moves back, does not look intentional. Pollard appeals for obstruction of the field. The umpire takes it upstairs with the SOFT SIGNAL BEING OUT! Time for the replays and it shows that Gunathilaka did not know where the ball exactly was. He does kick it though as he tries to come back into the crease. He does have a glance down at the ball but it seems like he does so after kicking it. The third umpire though rules it in the decision of the fielding side. A slightly harsh call!
The umpires will check if there was an obstruction for a run out! The soft signal, by the umpires, is OUT! The third umpire has a couple of looks at this and decides this will be OUT!
5 off the over! Shortish on middle, worked through square leg for a single.
Outside off, slapped to point.
Gives this one air and lands it around off, clipped through mid-wicket for one. The debutant is underway now!
On middle, defended.
Goes on the back foot to whip this one through mid-wicket. Rotates the strike.
The paddle sweep is out. Played through short fine leg for a couple!

A slower back of a length ball outside off, Nissanka waits and waits......and waits some more to finally attempt to play the upper cut. But gets decieved by the lack of pace. A dot to end an eventful over.
Around off, guided to point.
On a good length outside off, Danushka Gunathilaka plays this one uppish towards the cover region for one.
Leg bye. On a shorter length and around off, Pathum Nissanka looks to pull but the ball takes the helmet and goes to the off side for a leg bye.
Pathum Nissanka, the man on debut, walks out to bat!

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! THAT IS A BLINDER! Elation for Kieron Pollard! He has come on and has grabbed the first wicket of the game, when all the cards were against the Men in Maroon. His teammates surround him and will be finally happy to have broken this stand. A length delivery, a slower one too, Dimuth Karunaratne comes down the track and chips this one back towards KP! There is where Pollard shows his reaction time and athleticism as he hops and grabs this one with hand, the ball pops out, but he streches hard and goes, looking for second time luck. He does really well to hold this second time around. Success for WI!
PLAY AND A MISS! Pollard starts off with angling a length delivery outside off, Dimuth Karunaratne looks to have a feel of this but he fails to get any bat on this.
A single to end! On middle, this is worked through mid-wicket for one.

NOT OUT! 50 for the Lankan skipper now! First game here in the Windies and he scores a half ton. His 6th in ODIs! He too would want to bat for long now. This is shorter and outside off, it is placed behind point. The call is for two and they go for it. The fielder fires it to the keeper who whips the bails off and appeals. It is referred upstairs. Replays show that Karunaratne is in.
Two taken! On middle, this is hit nice and straight towards long on for two.

There is the single Gunathilaka was itching for! His fifty is up. 9th in ODIs! Solid knock from him so far but can he make it big? He is looking good and has the chance. He gets there by playing the paddle scoop on the leg side for one. The 100 is also up. The foundation has been laid by the openers for a big score.
Run out appeal taken upstairs now! Seems close but it does look like the bat is inside the crease as the bails are whipped off.
Another dot by Gunathilaka! On off, it is guided to point.
Karunaratne looks to play the paddle sweep, he tries to drag it from outside off. It goes off the inner half, onto the pads and on the leg side for one.
Superb from Walsh! That keeps Gunathilaka on 49! Shorter and outside off, Danushka cuts but the fielder at point dives to his right and makes a good stop.
Shorter and outside off, a slower one. Gunathilaka slaps it to covers.
For a second Gunathilaka did not know where the ball is! Slower one outside off, Gunathilaka looks to drive but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It is beside him. He wanted a run but is sent back.
Shortish again, this is nudged on the leg side for one.
Shorter and outside off, this is cut hard towards point. The fielder makes a half stop. A single.
Shorter and on middle, this is pulled through mid-wicket for one.

DRINKS BREAK. What a start this has been for the visitors. They have maintained their tempo and played attacking shots, at will and have done well to lead Sri Lanka to a score of 95/0 at the end of the 17th over. Both of them are closing in on their fifties and will look to continue this smart cricket for as long as they can. The hosts, meanwhile, will be looking around, hoping that one of their bowlers break this duo, which further, they will hope will open the floodgates.
A dot to end! On the pads, this is worked to short fine leg.
One more single! On middle, this is worked through square leg for one.
Karunaratne shuffles across but Akeal bowls it faster and on off, defended.
Another one on middle, Gunathilaka works it through mid-wicket for one more.
Flatter and on middle, this is pushed down to long on for one.
Outside off, slightly shorter, this is cut through point for one.
No, but just the one from the over! Windies need a few more like these to build the pressure. Shorter and outside off, this is slapped through covers for one.
Outside off, Gunathilaka guides it to point. Can this be a maiden?
Make that 4! Outside off, not played at.
A good slower one, it is guided to point. Three dots in a row.
Outside off, Gunathilaka waits for it and then guides it to gully.
On off, defended.
This time he does connect with a sweep but just one towards deep square leg.
Gunathilaka now looks to take on Hosein. He plays the sweep but this one lands outside off, turns back in and there is extra bounce. Hits Gunathilaka on the body.
On middle, this is pushed down to long on for one.
Well fielded! Shorter and outside off, this is guided to the left of point. Pooran there gets to the ball quickly, dives and stops it. Saves a run.
FOUR! Innovation and it comes off! The reverse sweep is out. It is hit nice and fine on the off side. Races away. So maybe Karunaratne has decided to take a few chances.
The paddle sweep is played, fine on the leg side for one.

Safe! First sign of aggression. Karunaratne takes a few steps down the track. It is a slower one from Holder. Dimuth looks to hit it over mid on but it hits the splice and lands short of the fielder there.
Confusion again but run taken in the end! On off, this is guided towards short third man. There is confusion between the two batters as to whether to take the run or no, they take it in the end.
Shorter and around off, Karunaratne pushes it to the left of mid off for one.
On middle, this is worked towards mid-wicket for no runs.
Two again! Shortish and outside off, Karunaratne guides it through point.
Outside off, Gunathilaka guides it down to third man for one more.
A dot to end! On off, this is pushed to the right of the bowler who moves across nicely and stops it.
Outside off, Gunathilaka slaps it through covers for one.
Confusion but no harm done! On off, this is pushed towards cover. Gunathilaka wants a run and is halfway down the wicket. Sent back in time. Just in time actually.
Milking the singles! On middle, this is eased down to long on.
On off, this is pushed down to long off for one.
On middle, this is worked down to long on for one.
Jason Mohammed is on!

DROPPED AND FOUR! Another caught and bowled chance not taken! This was hit back really hard though! Gunathilaka comes down the wicket and smashes it back towards the bowler. Shepherd looks to take it but the ball once again bursts out and this time it races away to the long off fence. This needed to stick. So a chance for both the batters as of now.
This is worked with the angle through square leg for another boundary.
FOUR! This is delightful! Just a mere push! Length and around off, it is hit on the up, past mid off and into the fence.
Drop and run! This has been the stand out between the two. Yes, they have hit a lot of boundaries but the running between the wickets has been excellent! On off, it is dropped towards cover for one.
On the pads, Karunaratne works it to fine leg for one.

DROPPED! Shepherd has put down a chance of his own bowling! He may have not been expecting it. This is a length ball outside off, Karunaratne looks to push it on the off side but the ball comes slow off the surface. It goes back off the inner half towards Shepherd who is late in reacting. It bursts through his hands and goes to mid on. It should have been taken and Windies needed that to be caught.
On middle, it is pushed down to long on for another single.
This is fired on the stumps, Karunaratne is hurried into the stroke. He plays it back to the bowler.
Gunathilaka comes down the track and works it through mid-wicket for one.
On the pads, this is worked through square leg for one.
Flatter and on off, Danushka pushes it towards cover for one.
On the pads, Gunathilaka works it to short fine leg.
Another wide! One more ball down the leg side, Gunathilaka looks to flick but misses. The bowler is appealing but he is the only one doing so.
WIDE! Bowls this one down the leg side, DG looks to flick but misses. Wided.
Time for Powerplay 2! Now a maximum of 4 fielders can be placed outside the ring till the 40th over.
One more dot to end! On middle, it is worked to mid-wicket. End of a good Powerplay 1 for Lanka!
Better from Shepherd! On off, from over the wicket. Length, it is pushed to mid off.
Another single! Sheperd comes around the wicket and bangs it shorter and on the body, this is worked on the leg side for one.
Three this time! Full and outside off, DK plays it through covers. Not right off the middle, it stops as it gets closer to the ropes.
Another one full and outside off, Karunaratne gets bat on ball and hits it through covers. Two!
Almost strikes on the first ball! This is well wide outside off. Karunaratne goes after it but misses.
Another single to end! A tidy start by Hosein. On the pads, this is worked through square leg for one.
Fifty up for Lanka! This is a very good start by their openers! Started off slowly but have recovered really well. On middle, this is pushed down to long on for one.
Fuller and on middle, this is worked down to long on for one.
Close! Shorter and quicker outside off. Karunaratne looks to cut but it is a little close. Gets beaten.
Two taken! Comes down the track and works it with the turn through square leg.
Some turn for him! Flatter and on middle, it turns back in. It is worked to mid-wicket.
Change in bowling! Spin introduced as Akeal Hosein comes on!
Better from Holder but it is another expensive over! Gets his line and length right on the last ball! Outside off, left alone.
A rare dot! On off, defended.
Two! Runs coming along nicely now! Outside off, this is played late through backward point for two.

FOUR! This is deft! 5 boundaries in the last 5 balls and 8 in total. This is lovely! Lets the ball come to him. This is quite close to the off pole. Gunathilaka waits for it and then guides it past the fielder who is quite fine at short third man. Goes to the third man fence.
FOUR! Through the off side this time! Raining boundaries here! This is short and wide outside off, this is slapped through covers. No chance of stopping it.
FOUR! Gunathilaka now joins the action! Three boundaries in a row for Lanka! Shorter again, it is pulled through mid-wicket. Pollard will not be happy with the lengths bowled here.

FOUR! Third boundary in the over and that is the welcome big over which the Lankans needed! Once again it is a little too short and it bounces at a good hieght for the batter. He pulls it through mid-wicket.

FOUR! Was that a chance? The fielder did not react quickyl It was hit really hard though! Shorter and on middle, this is pulled uppishly towards square leg. The fielder does put his hands up to take it but does so late. Another boundary.
Uppish but away from the fielder! On the pads, Karunaratne works it through square leg and takes two.
Excellent stuff! Lets the ball come to him and then drops it on the off side with soft hands. Takes one.

FOUR! Caressed! This is important, when runs are hard to come by, you need to put the bad balls away and DG does that. It is fuller and outside off, Gunathilaka smashes it through covers for a boundary.
Outside off, it is played to the man at point. This is a sedate start from the two openers.
Lovely delivery to end a brilliant over! Length, slightly on the fuller side. Angles it away. Karunaratne is drawn into the drive. It whizzes past the outside edge.
5 dots in a row! On middle, this is pushed to the man at mid on.
Another dot! This is good tight bowling! On off, Karunaratne pushes it to covers.
On middle, this is worked to mid on.
Outside off, angling away. Some extra bounce too. Karunaratne slashes but misses.
Around off, Karunaratne guides it to point.
Good bumper to end! On the body, Gunathilaka gets out of the way in time. A sharp over from Joseph. He is getting some good bounce off the surface.
On middle, Karunaratne pushes it towards mid on for one.
That has taken off! Shortish and on the body, rises after landing. Gunathilaka fends at it awkwardly. It goes off the glove and on the leg side for one. He was lucky that did not pop up.
Back of a length and on off, defended.
Hits it well but no runs! Shorter and outside off, it is slapped but to covers. It is a packed off side field.

FOUR! EDGED AND OVER! Gunathilaka slashes hard there. It is on a length and angling across. Danushka goes after it. It flies off the outside edge and goes over the second slip fielder. This is not a wicket where you can hit on the up.
On off, Karnaratne drops it on the off side. He wants one but is sent back.
On a length again, it is defended.
On the pads, karunaratne looks to flick but misses to get hit high on the pads.
Good batting! Follows the boundary with a single as this is pushed to mid off.
FOUR! Cut away! First boundary and probably the first ball that si timed well. Shorter and outside off. Gunathilaka lets the ball come to him this time and then cuts it through point for a boundary.
Length again and on off, Gunathilaka looks to push hard at it but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
An effort delivery to end! On middle, DK stands tall and keeps it out. Three tidy vers to begin with by Windies.
No timing on that one as well! Shorter and outside off, it is not coming off that nicely. The cut shot is mistimed to mid off.
Shorter and outside off, Karunaratne looks to push at it but it once again goes off the inner half back to the bowler.
Once again Karunaratne not getting the timing right. On off and on a length, it is pushed to mid off.
Uppish but in the gap! That one sticks in the surface! It is shorter and outside off, Karnaratne looks to cut at first but then plays a check-shot. It goes wide of covers for two.
Slightly shorter in length and outside off, Karunaratne looks to push at it but gets it off the inner half, back to the bowler.
A good start by Holder! On off, this is pushed to covers.
On the fuller side, it tails back in a little but not enough to make the batter play.
Extra bounce! Holder bends his back on this one, it is outside off and on a length. Takes off after pitching. Gunathilaka is beaten as he tries to push at it.
Good length and on middle, it is solidly blocked.
A single as this is worked towards mid-wicket.
On the pads, Karunaratne looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. A muted appeal but turned down.
Jason Holder to bowl from the other end!
A single to end! A quiet first over then! Shoter and on middle, Karunaratne mistimes his pull towards mid-wicket for one.
Outside off, left alone.
Gunathilaka is underway! Length and outside off, it is guided towards third man for one.
Back of a length and on off, it is pushed to mid off.
Shorter and outside off, comes onto the bat nicely. It is guided to point.
Well bowled! Gets it right, it is on off, comes back in a little. Gunathilaka looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
WIDE! Sri Lanka  are underway courtesy an extra! This is well wide outside off, it is left alone. Wided.

We are all set for the action to begin! The Sri Lankan openers, Dimuth Karunaratne, Danushka Gunathilaka walk out to the middle. Alzarri Joseph to begin proceedings with the first new ball. Here we go...

Samuel Badree doing the pitch report says there is a strong breeze, the average first innings score is 241. Ambrose says it looks a decent surface, he expected more grass on it but it seems a hard surface, adds there might be some extra bounce but it should be good for batting.
WINDIES (PLAYING XI) - Shai Hope (WK), Evin Lewis, Jason Mohammed, Darren Bravo, Nicholas Pooran, Kieron Pollard (C), Jason Holder, Fabian Allen, Romario Shepherd, Alzarri Joseph, Akeal Hosein.

SRI LANKAN (PLAYING XI) - Dimuth Karunaratne (C), Danushka Gunathilaka, Pathum Nissanka, Dinesh Chandimal (WK), Angelo Mathews, Ashen Bandara, Kamindu Mendis, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dushmantha Chameera, Lakshan Sandakan, Nuwan Pradeep.

Windies skipper, Kieron Pollard, says they need to bat well, this is a longer format so they need to apply themselves. Informs Darren Bravo, Joseph, Hope and Sheperd come into the side. Ends by saying they have practiced well and he hopes they can do well here.
Lankan captain, Dimuth Karunaratne, says they have got a couple of practice sessions and are confident. Ends by saying they hope to put up a good score on the board.
TOSS - SRI LANKA HAVE WON THE TOSS AND OPTED TO BAT!

After an exciting T20I series it is now time to turn your attention towards the 50-over format. It was the hosts who won the T20i series and the Windies would want to come out on top here too. Sri Lanka will also be hungry to come out victorious so that they can head 1-1 into the Test series which follows. The Sri Lankans probably have a better chance in this format than in the shortest one but Windies, playing at home, are still favoritues. Welcome to the coevrage. Saty tuned for the toss...
